summary: On node1, cron scheduling is now restricted to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow. opsadmin user was created (did not previously exist). Verified via a throwaway test user that non-listed users are denied by crontab, and that opsadmin/root are permitted, both before and after a full node restart (boot_id changed from f9bf293d... to 72810ce8...), confirming persistence and cron service recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/cron package/service and confirmed no /etc/cron.allow or /etc/cron.deny existed, and opsadmin user did not exist
Created opsadmin user (locked password, home dir) on node1
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin', root:root owned, mode 644; removed any stray /etc/cron.deny
Verified root and opsadmin can use crontab (list and install a job), then cleaned up the test job
Created and used a throwaway low-priv test user to confirm crontab denies non-listed users, then deleted that test user
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cron/cron.allow/opsadmin state as baseline
Issued a native reboot on node1 (single node) with acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again and confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart
Re-verified post-restart: cron service active, /etc/cron.allow and opsadmin persisted, opsadmin allowed, a fresh ephemeral test user denied, then removed that test user

evidence.requirement: Baseline: no pre-existing cron.allow/cron.deny, opsadmin absent
evidence.summary: Confirmed /etc/cron.allow and /etc/cron.deny did not exist and opsadmin user did not exist prior to changes

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: Created /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin; demonstrated root and opsadmin can use crontab (list/install job) while a non-listed test user (crontest) is explicitly denied with 'You (crontest) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)'; cleaned up test user and temp job

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service health) for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3, cron service active, cron.allow contents, and opsadmin existence before restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued native 'reboot' via backgrounded sudo command; 'reboot-acknowledged' returned to the caller before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof of actual restart via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection reset confirmed the node went down; subsequent poll succeeded with boot_id changed to 72810ce8-b39f-4307-a33a-450cd2387bf3 and new uptime, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service, cron.allow restriction, and opsadmin account
evidence.summary: After restart, cron service active, /etc/cron.allow still contains root/opsadmin, opsadmin account persists and can use crontab, and a freshly created ephemeral test user is still denied by crontab (then removed), confirming the restriction survived the restart
